PulseChain GRT gateway: mint transaction and allowance
reconciliation
This read-only audit establishes how the GRT destination gateway funded a completed withdrawal on
PulseChain. It distinguishes the destination evidence from the historical source-chain design. The
bounded event census ends at block 27,659,393, hash 
0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275. It makes no finding about participants'
motives, human identities or an independently operating pARB network.
Recorded transaction
Transaction 0xf7ed5701901cef056395582eab068f1a2e75cdfcf717301c16e89a05ff885ae9 succeeded at block 
27,434,949, 1 September 2026 13:42:05 UTC. Its block hash is 
0xbc7a6608cbb7515daaa1464f02cf94fc162b9f89c8c7a0a2859d140c575dd4bb.
Item Observed value
Transaction sender 0xfbba783afda7b41ebb7473a914f0b6eb9f9139f3
Transaction target / outbox 0x0b9857ae2d4a3dbe74ffe1d7df045bb7f96e4840
Bridge 0x8315177ab297ba92a06054ce80a67ed4dbd7ed3a
GRT gateway 0x01cdc91b0a9ba741903aa3699bf4ce31d6c5cc06
Gateway implementation actually called 0xd41ca6a1d034d178c196dfa916f22f7d1a1b8222
GRT token 0xc944e90c64b2c07662a292be6244bdf05cda44a7
GRT escrow 0x36aff7001294dae4c2ed4fdefc478a00de77f090
Recipient and event's source-account field 0xa0b347117a878da9942fa5c31b87c773a2969913
Withdrawal amount 62,875,937.675361278837595998 GRT
Existing escrow contribution 1 GRT
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 82

Item Observed value
Newly minted shortfall 62,875,936.675361278837595998 GRT
Escrow balance after transaction block 0 GRT
The actual trace, rather than only present implementation storage, identifies the implementation used
for this transaction. The gateway reads the escrow's balance, calls GraphToken.mint(escrow, shortfall), and
then calls transferFrom(escrow, recipient, withdrawalAmount). The receipt contains both the zero-address mint
transfer and the full outgoing escrow transfer. The previously retained total-supply comparison matches
the shortfall exactly.
The accounting reconciliation is therefore:
1 existing GRT + 62,875,936.675361278837595998 minted GRT = 62,875,937.675361278837595998 delivered GRT.
The trace's source-sender getter returns configured counterpart 0x65e1a5e8946e7e87d9774f5288f41c30a99fd302.
This establishes the destination checks and calls that succeeded; it does not independently prove the
origin of the message or a source-chain burn.
The allowance was inherited and accumulated with block height
The complete selected configuration-event query, block 0 through the audit endpoint, returned six
receipt-verified events with no query errors: four initial address-setting events, one allowance update,
and the one mint event. There were no post-fork selected configuration events. This statement is
bounded to those addresses, signatures, range and RPC results; it is not an exhaustive audit of all ways
proxy or contract state could change.
The allowance update is transaction 0x44d5c8a62f2a790f2d7f8238c66df042d500e1b429ffb0bc2f9724009817907d, block 
17,071,882, 18 April 2023 06:45:23 UTC, before the fork. Its emitted parameters are:
Accumulated allowance snapshot: 0 GRT.
Accrual rate: 6.0365 GRT per block.
Effective starting block: 17,018,986. This differs from the transaction's block.
Getter-only reads at inherited block 17,232,999, transaction-predecessor block 27,434,948 and
transaction block 27,434,949 return the same three parameters. GraphToken.isMinter(gateway) returns true
at all three snapshots. The inherited and predecessor cumulative minted amounts are zero; the
transaction-block value equals the recorded shortfall.
For transaction block b = 27,434,949, the verified gateway formula gives:
allowance(b) = 0 + 6.0365 × (27,434,949 − 17,018,986) = 62,875,960.6495 GRT.
Subtracting the transaction's cumulative minted amount leaves 23.974138721162404002 GRT of
unused allowance at that block. The later endpoint allowance of 64,230,816.8555 GRT leaves 
1,354,880.180138721162404002 GRT. These are GRT quantities under the recorded accounting rule,
not dollar amounts or a guarantee of another withdrawal.
This evidence supports use of inherited mint permission and block-accrued capacity. It does not
support saying that a post-fork actor increased the GRT mint rate. The block-based formula does not
itself observe actual source-chain rewards or custody.

Both post-fork GRT withdrawals
The gateway's WithdrawalFinalized(address,address,address,uint256,uint256) query covers blocks 17,233,000–
27,659,393. It returned exactly two events, with receipt inclusion, successful status and block-hash
consistency verified and no query errors.
Date UTC Transaction Amount and disposition
8 January 2025 06:18:05 0xd35b3809e5551a1972b518cd38baf0936
63edddcac26b8c9792ac1d0d7b71093
30,490,952.885900226731295138
GRT transferred from escrow to 
0xb8698cfffdaaf26ca21fe8aa560c18cc2
b2f5996; no GRT mint transfer in this
receipt.
1 September 2026 13:42:05 0xf7ed5701901cef056395582eab068f1a2
e75cdfcf717301c16e89a05ff885ae9
62,875,937.675361278837595998
GRT delivered, funded by 1 existing
GRT and the new mint described
above.
The January withdrawal amount equals the escrow balance read at the inherited snapshot. Equality does
not by itself prove that no intermediate deposits or withdrawals occurred. The two recipient addresses
are factual observations; common ownership is not established by these events.
Escrow transfer ledger and the origin of the remaining 1 GRT
A follow-up query of all post-fork GRT Transfer logs into and out of the exact escrow returned two
incoming and two outgoing events through the same endpoint. The first incoming event was not a mint.
On 8 January 2025 at 05:13:55 UTC, wallet 0xb8698cfffdaaf26ca21fe8aa560c18cc2b2f5996 called the GRT
token and transferred 1 GRT into escrow in transaction 0xa9848625…, block 22,391,830. Receipt
success, event inclusion and block/transaction hashes were verified. Historical balance getters reconcile
the sequence:
Point in the observed history Escrow GRT
Block 22,391,829, before the deposit 30,490,952.885900226731295138
Block 22,391,830, after the 1-GRT deposit 30,490,953.885900226731295138
Block 22,392,214, before the January withdrawal 30,490,953.885900226731295138
Block 22,392,215, after the January withdrawal 1
Immediately before the September mint, as read in its
trace
1
After the September mint and full outgoing transfer 0
Thus the observed escrow ledger reconciles from its inherited balance through the two withdrawals: the
January deposit added 1 GRT, the January withdrawal left that amount, and the September transaction
combined it with newly minted GRT. The two incoming/outgoing log queries returned no other post-fork
escrow transfers in this range. These are address-level token movements, not evidence of the
depositor's purpose or ownership of the September recipient.
The new manifests are Research/experiments/parb_grt_escrow_ledger_20260929.json and Research/experiments/
parb_grt_escrow_reconciliation_20260929.json. They preserve exact read-only request parameters; raw
responses, receipt, headers, transaction and historical balance reads are under ignored artifacts/parb-
grt-escrow-ledger-20260929/, with a SHA-256 manifest.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 84

Historical source design: burn on L2, then release or mint on L1
The official GIP-0037 predates the fork and describes L2 indexing-reward issuance plus bounded L1
gateway minting when withdrawals exceed escrow. Its allowance follows linear block-based accrual. This
is a protocol-specific accommodation for L2-native GRT issuance, not a generic permission to mint
arbitrary tokens.
The official repository's L2 gateway at commit 68f70769803e03db6da78d8b89e1af23aad303cd, dated 5 May 2023,
calls bridgeBurn on the sending account during outboundTransfer. That source describes burn on L2
followed by escrow release and, if necessary, authorized shortfall minting on L1. It is not a
design in which the very same withdrawable GRT remains locked or invested on L2 while being issued
again on L1.
The historical official source explains the mechanism; it is not a verified pARB runtime or source-chain
transaction. No independently accessible pARB source-state record was supplied for this transaction. The
audited destination mint stands independently of that missing source observation.
Effect on the main paper
GRT is a second observed destination-issuance case beyond ARB, using a different accounting
mechanism. The paper should state that a lack of sufficient L1 escrow does not universally prevent
withdrawal: this GRT gateway filled a real shortfall using pre-existing token mint authority, within its
allowance.
The finding does not establish that every gateway mints, that a stablecoin gateway can use GRT's
permission, that a source position remains invested, or that issued GRT was subsequently accepted as
collateral or exchanged into pDAI. Each of those would require its own address-specific transaction
evidence. The factual contribution is an executed, quantitatively reconciled example of a specialized
issuer-aware bridge.
Reproduction references
The maintained manifests are:
parb_grt_allowance_events_20260929.json.
parb_grt_withdrawal_events_20260929.json.
parb_grt_historical_getters_20260929.json.
Run the event manifests with Research/scripts/collect_pulsechain_events.py --manifest <manifest> --output
<new-output>. Run the getter manifest with Research/scripts/probe_pulsechain_routes.py --calls <manifest> --
block <hex-block> --output <new-output> at 0x106f467, 0x1a29fc4 and 0x1a29fc5. Both collectors refuse to
overwrite an existing output.
New raw results, historical official source and arithmetic reconciliation are retained under ignored 
artifacts/parb-grt-mint-reconciliation-20260929/, with a SHA-256 manifest linking the prior transaction
evidence. The broader source and routing census is documented in
[parb_bridge_mint_inventory_20260929.md (Appendix 4) (Appendix 4)](#appendix-04). No state-
changing call or transaction was made.
